title: publish-release.sh's closing message is hardcoded to 0.3.5 and retired tmux panes
description: scripts/publish-release.sh ends with a quoted heredoc that tells the operator, on EVERY release, to cut a GitHub Release for v0.3.5 using CHANGELOG's [0.3.5] section and to message tmux panes wK:pR and wS:pK, citing LCLI-363's acceptance criteria. All of it is stale: 0.3.5 shipped long ago, LCLI-363 is closed, and pane addressing belongs to the retired Treehouse-era workflow -- sessions are addressed by name via ListAgents now and names change on every restart. Observed live during the 0.6.1 publish on 2026-09-13. The defect is not the wrong values but that they are hardcoded at all: a quoted heredoc cannot interpolate $VERSION, so it was guaranteed to go stale the moment 0.3.5 shipped and will do so again for any fixed version. Fix by deriving the message from $VERSION and removing perishable references (specific task ids, pane addresses) entirely.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The closing message names the version actually being published, derived from $VERSION, so it cannot go stale again
No task id, tmux pane, or fixed version number appears in the closing message
Downstream notification step says to resolve session names with ListAgents rather than naming addresses that change on restart, and includes the opum-marketplace skills/ tree SHA obligation
A manual publish is called out as producing no provenance attestation, since that is now a real possibility per LCLI-482

finalSummary:
Delivered by PR #15 (commit 10e75653) on 2026-09-13 and left open; closing on verified evidence rather than on the commit message.

Checked each criterion against the code on dev, not against the commit subject:
  AC#0 -- scripts/publish-release.sh's closing heredoc is now unquoted and opens 'PUBLISHED $VERSION'; every reference in it interpolates (v$VERSION, CHANGELOG's [$VERSION] section, git ls-tree v$VERSION skills). It cannot go stale for a fixed version again, which was the actual defect -- not the wrong values but that they were hardcoded at all.
  AC#1 -- no task id, no tmux pane address, no fixed version number anywhere in the closing message.
  AC#2 -- step 3 tells the operator to resolve each downstream session with ListAgents and match on repository, warns that names change on every restart, and carries the opum-marketplace obligation to hand over the resolved skills/ tree SHA (git ls-tree v$VERSION skills) or its federated-content check goes red.
  AC#3 -- step 4 requires recording HOW the version shipped, and says that a version published by this script rather than the OIDC job carries NO provenance attestation because a manual publish cannot produce one, with an explicit warning not to let a reader infer provenance from an earlier version having it. That criterion turned out to be load-bearing: 0.6.1 shipped exactly this way.

NOT CHANGED, deliberately: the literal 0.3.5 strings remaining at the top of the file are in the header comment that describes the historical defect and in the usage examples. AC#1 scopes to the closing message, and rewriting the comment that records what went wrong would erase the reason the fix exists.

Observed live during the 0.6.1 publish, which is how it was found.



ADDENDUM, same session: the usage examples WERE refreshed after all, at the orchestrator's request, and my note above that they were left alone is superseded for that half. They are now PLACEHOLDERS (<version> <run-id>) rather than a newer hardcoded pair -- which is the same lesson as the original defect. Substituting 0.6.1 and a real run id would have restarted exactly the staleness clock this task exists to stop; a placeholder cannot go stale.

The header comment at line 226 is still untouched and still names 0.3.5, deliberately: it is the record of what went wrong, and rewriting it would erase why the fix exists.

One trap worth recording because it is invisible: line 41 prints usage with 'sed -n "2,34p"', addressing the header by LINE NUMBER. Any edit inside lines 2-34 that changes the line COUNT silently truncates or overruns the usage output. The replacement was made three-lines-for-three-lines and the file is still 255 lines; verified by running the script with no arguments and reading what it actually printed, not by inspecting the source.
